identification.summary: Iranian destructive cyber actor that Microsoft tracked as DEV-0842 (now Storm-0842), the cluster that deployed ransomware and a wiper against the Albanian government on 15 July 2022 [S1]. Check Point tracks the activity as Void Manticore, a MOIS-affiliated group that runs the 'Homeland Justice' persona against Albania and the 'Karma' persona against Israel and uses custom wipers [S4]. Later vendor reporting ties the 'Handala' hack-and-leak persona to the same cluster, including the March 2026 Intune-based mass wipe at Stryker [S7][S8].
identification.firstObserved: Destructive deployment by DEV-0842 against Albania on 2022-07-15. Microsoft says other Iranian clusters held access from May 2021 [S1]. Mandiant saw a ROADSWEEP ransomware sample from Albania on 2022-07-22 [S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name in this record: Red Sandstorm. The Microsoft sources gathered here use DEV-0842/Storm-0842 [S1], and secondary 2026 reporting says Microsoft tracks the Handala cluster as Storm-0842 [S7][S8]. Microsoft splits the 2022 Albania operation across several clusters: DEV-0861 (initial access, mail exfiltration), DEV-0166 (mail exfiltration), DEV-0133 (probing) and DEV-0842 (ransomware and wiper) [S1]. Only the DEV-0842 role belongs to this record. Check Point describes a handoff in which Scarred Manticore gains access and then passes targets to Void Manticore [S4]. CrowdStrike's name is Banished Kitten [S7].

attribution.sponsor: Iran, Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS), per Check Point's assessment of Void Manticore [S4]. FBI and CISA attribute the 2022 Albania attacks to 'Iranian state cyber actors' [S2].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft has high confidence that Iranian government-sponsored actors carried out the 15 July 2022 destructive attack [S1]. Microsoft has moderate confidence that the initial-access and exfiltration actors are linked to EUROPIUM, which is publicly tied to MOIS [S1]. Mandiant made a moderate-confidence assessment that one or more actors operating in support of Iranian goals were involved, but tied the activity to no named group [S3]. Check Point links Void Manticore to MOIS [S4]. The Handala-to-Void Manticore link is a vendor assessment that secondary sources credit to Check Point in May 2024 [S7][S8].
attribution.basis: Microsoft incident response and telemetry [S1]; FBI investigation summarized in Joint Cybersecurity Advisory AA22-264A [S2]; Mandiant malware and persona analysis [S3]; Check Point research on overlaps in wipers and personas [S4]; secondary vendor analyses of the 2026 Stryker incident [S7][S8].

objectives: Disruptive and destructive attacks combined with hack-and-leak influence operations that punish and intimidate states and organizations opposed to Iranian policy. These include Albania for hosting the MEK [S1][S3] and Israeli organizations [S4]. Microsoft assessed the 2022 Albania attack as retaliation for cyberattacks on Iran that Tehran blamed on Israel and the MEK [S1]. Handala claimed the 2026 Stryker attack as retaliation for a reported US strike [S8].

regions: United States-headquartered multinationals with global device fleets (Stryker, 2026) [S7][S8]
targeting.notes: Reporting says the Karma persona claimed attacks on more than 40 Israeli organizations [S4].

capabilities.summary: In Albania (July 2022), DEV-0842 deployed GoXml.exe ransomware and the cl.exe wiper, which uses the RawDisk driver rwdsk.sys. It also used a Defender-disabling tool and the Mellona.exe SMB distributor. Web shells, Mimikatz and Impacket were seen in the wider intrusion [S1]. FBI/CISA report that the actors deployed a ZeroCleare variant after defenders responded to the ransomware [S2]. Check Point-based reporting names custom wipers: CI Wiper and No-Justice/LowEraser in Albania, and an updated BiBi wiper with partition-table deletion in Israel [S4]. In 2026 the cluster shifted to abusing living-off-the-cloud administration. Reporting describes AiTM phishing and infostealer-derived session tokens used to compromise an Intune administrator, the creation of a new Global Administrator, and Microsoft Graph API calls that issued mass factory resets without custom malware [S7]. Hack-and-leak through Telegram personas and websites is a constant feature [S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Albania government destructive attack (Homeland Justice)
campaigns.summary: On 15 July, DEV-0842 deployed ransomware and a wiper that disrupted Albanian government websites and public services. Initial access, gained by other clusters through SharePoint CVE-2019-0604, dated to May 2021. The Homeland Justice persona leaked data and pushed anti-MEK messaging.

campaigns.name: Second Albania wave and US advisory
campaigns.summary: FBI/CISA report further Iranian destructive activity against Albania in September 2022, likely as retaliation for public attribution and the severing of diplomatic ties. The advisory notes about 14 months of prior access and use of a ZeroCleare variant.

campaigns.name: Karma persona attacks on Israeli organizations
campaigns.summary: Check Point-based reporting says the Karma persona claimed attacks on more than 40 Israeli organizations using an updated BiBi wiper, posting stolen data or evidence of wiped drives on Telegram.

campaigns.name: Check Point public exposure of Void Manticore
campaigns.summary: Check Point publishes research linking Homeland Justice and Karma to MOIS-affiliated Void Manticore and describing target handoff from Scarred Manticore.

campaigns.name: Stryker Intune mass-wipe (Handala)
campaigns.summary: On 11 March 2026, attackers using the Handala persona reportedly compromised Stryker's Intune administration and factory-reset a large device fleet. Device counts reach about 200,000 in some reports, and Stryker said no malware was found.

diamond.adversary: Iranian MOIS-affiliated destructive unit (Microsoft DEV-0842/Storm-0842; Check Point Void Manticore; CrowdStrike Banished Kitten) operating the Homeland Justice, Karma and Handala personas [S1][S4][S7].
diamond.capability: Custom wipers and ransomware (cl.exe, GoXml, ZeroCleare variant, CI Wiper, No-Justice/LowEraser, BiBi) [S1][S2][S4]; credential tools and web shells [S1]; in 2026, Intune and Graph API remote wipe through a compromised administrator identity [S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channels and persona websites used for leaks and claims [S3][S4]; access handed off from partner MOIS clusters (Scarred Manticore; EUROPIUM-linked actors in Albania) [S1][S4]; victim cloud management planes used as the delivery mechanism [S7].
diamond.victim: Albanian government and public services [S1][S2]; Israeli organizations [S4]; the global medtech firm Stryker [S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Retaliation tied to Albania hosting the MEK and to Israel/US conflict with Iran, amplified through influence messaging [S1][S3][S8].
diamond.technology: Windows domain environments, on-premises SharePoint (initial access by partner clusters), and cloud endpoint management (Microsoft Intune/Entra ID) [S1][S7].

gaps: Could not confirm in any source that Microsoft uses the name 'Red Sandstorm'. learn.microsoft.com could not be fetched. The cited Microsoft and secondary sources use DEV-0842/Storm-0842. A Wikipedia article (Handala Hack Team) surfaced in search with the alias 'Red Sandstorm' and attributes it to Iran International reporting, but the article could not be opened or dated.

Primary documents not opened: CISA/FBI AA22-264A (cisa.gov blocked), the Check Point Void Manticore and 'Bad Karma, No Justice' reports (fetch failed), the Mandiant ROADSWEEP blog, Unit 42's Handala wiper report, and Microsoft's March 2026 Intune hardening guidance. Details come from search-result coverage.
Microsoft assigns initial access in Albania to other clusters (DEV-0861, EUROPIUM-linked). Do not credit access-phase TTPs to Storm-0842 without checking.
Mandiant did not confirm that ROADSWEEP was the ransomware used in the government attack, and tied the activity to no named group [S3].

Stryker impact figures (device counts, 61 vs 79 countries, a 50 TB exfiltration claim) conflict across secondary sources and are unverified. One vendor claims MuddyWater pre-positioned access before the wipe; this is single-source.

Reported link between the unit and sanctioned MOIS deputy minister Yahya Hosseini Panjaki (and his reported 2026 death) comes only from Wikipedia citing Iran International. Treasury's September 2024 designation, as summarized in search results, concerns transnational repression, not cyber.
Sources disagree on whether the Karma persona was retired and replaced by Handala, or whether both were active at once.
First-activity date of the cluster before July 2022 is not established in public sources.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): Key terrain is identity and management planes, meaning domain controllers, Entra ID Global Administrator roles and Intune or other MDM consoles, which can be turned into fleet-wide wipe mechanisms [S7]. It also includes internet-facing collaboration servers that partner MOIS clusters exploit for initial access [S1]. STEP 2 (effects): Destruction is timed to political events (MEK conference, diplomatic disputes, kinetic conflict), and hack-and-leak amplifies the psychological effect [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 3 (threat model): A partner cluster gains long-dwell access (about 14 months in Albania) and exfiltrates mail; this unit then deploys ransomware-styled wipers or abuses MDM remote wipe, and a persona claims the attack on Telegram [S1][S2][S4][S7]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is a hack-and-leak plus wiper attack against government or regional partner-nation networks during periods of Iran-Israel/US tension [S4]. MDCOA is an identity-plane compromise of a defense contractor or mission partner leading to mass MDM wipe of endpoints that support operations, as at Stryker [S7]. Candidate indicators: creation of new Global Administrator accounts; bulk Intune wipe or retire actions through Graph API; RawDisk driver (rwdsk.sys) loading; Defender-disable tooling; Telegram persona claims naming the organization [S1][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: Track Handala, Homeland Justice and Karma persona channels as early warning, since claims and leaks accompany or follow attacks [S3][S4]. Watch for joint advisories on Iranian destructive activity [S2]. Authorities: Activity hits partner nations (Albania is a NATO member) and US companies, so response may require DCO coordination with mission partners and DIB/CISA/FBI channels rather than DoDIN-only actions [S2][S7]. Mission assurance: Enforce multi-admin approval and phishing-resistant MFA for MDM and identity admins, keep offline recovery for endpoints, and harden SharePoint and VPN edges used by access-broker clusters [S1][S7]. Coordination: Because access and destruction are split across MOIS clusters, hunt across the handoff boundary, so that detecting a partner's long-dwell access becomes a pre-strike warning for Storm-0842 effects [S1][S4].
